observations.summary: Repository pattern correctly separates data access from route handlers
observations.detail: The Repository<T> base class provides generic CRUD, batch findByIds (single IN-clause), and cursor-based pagination with prepared statements. Connection pool manages lifecycle with min/max sizing and idle reaping. Unit of work wraps transactions with auto-commit/rollback.

observations.summary: All 3 original performance optimizations preserved in refactor
observations.detail: Batch queries preserved via Repository.findByIds() using IN-clause instead of N+1. Cursor pagination preserved in Repository.list() with cursor + LIMIT. Prepared statements preserved via Connection.execute() with per-connection caching by statement name.

observations.summary: UserRepositoryAdapter provides sync backwards compatibility but should be temporary
observations.detail: The adapter accesses internal Maps directly for sync compat with existing route handlers. This creates a dual-write path where in-memory and DB state could diverge. Recommend setting migration deadline to convert callers to async UserRepository methods.

observations.summary: 36 new tests use real in-memory connections, not mocks
observations.detail: Tests cover connection pool (7), connection transactions (5), unit of work (8), user repository (8), adapter backwards compat (5), performance optimizations (3). All 106 total tests pass.

observations.summary: Connection pool lacks wait timeout on exhaustion
observations.detail: acquire() throws immediately when pool is exhausted. Consider adding configurable wait timeout that queues requests and retries when connections are released, rather than failing fast.

observations.summary: No query logging for production debugging
observations.detail: Adding optional query logging (SQL + params + duration) at the connection level would help trace N+1 regressions and slow queries in production.
